messages:
nina: FYI partner QA flagged that requests from PartnerY are intermittently charged to our infra project. Spike at 05:03 UTC. looks like attribution flip.

omar: Ugh. Do we have an example? header vs token claims?

nina: sample log: ```ts=2025-03-04 auth=ok token_kind=api_key claims_project= - header.X-Redwood-Project=partnery-321 routed_project=infra-staging```

sam: That implies header arrived but we still routed to fallback. Could be middleware ordering or a race in token parsing.

julie: We shipped router refactor last week that parallelizes auth validators. Possible the header injector runs after routing decision now.

ops-bot: alert: billing-attribution-anomaly triggered (5m avg >2%). Paging eng-platform.

omar: Immediate mitigations: 1) set unattributed_default=shared-billing-temp, 2) fail requests without attribution, 3) force header precedence for partner keys only.

sam: Option 3 is attractive but needs secure partner signing. For now I prefer 1 to avoid breaking partners.

julie: I'll push a quick hotfix to reorder middleware in canary (patch: move header injector before token parser). also adding unit test to catch regressions.

deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-router v3.2.1-canary -> 10% traffic. CI green.

nina: telemetry ask: emit `auth.attribution_source` ("claims"|"header"|"fallback") and `billing.attributed=true/false`. also add counter for `attribution_conflict` when header != claims.

omar: Agree; add a dashboard tile: attribution_source distribution + top-keys with fallback routing in last 1h.

sam: After canary: watch `billing.unattributed_count` and partner reported volume. If stable for 15m promote.

julie: Canary results: unattributed routing dropped from 4.8% -> 0.2% after reorder. promoting to 50%.

ops-bot: sampling for attribution traces set to 100% for 10m.

nina: Followups: (A) telemetry PR (omar) (B) partner signed-header proposal (sam+julie) (C) console banner for keys with recent unattributed billing (product).

omar: I'll open the telemetry PR and mock panels. thanks.

sam: thanks everyone. filing retro to discuss default fallback (should it ever bill a team?) :thinking_face:
